findings.title: Manifest paths can delete files outside the install root
findings.description: `finish()` joins stale paths read from the project’s `.context-forge/<target>.manifest` to `targetRoot` and may delete the result without checking containment. A crafted `../` path—or a path reached through a symlinked parent—can therefore delete an external file if its recorded checksum and size match. The new direct-install path runs this cleanup for project roots and worktrees; validate lexical and resolved-path containment before reading or deleting stale files.

findings.title: Dry runs can write through symlinks into real locations
findings.description: `copyInstallPaths()` preserves symlinks with `verbatimSymlinks: true`, then runs the installer against the sandbox. If an install directory such as `.claude/rules` is an absolute symlink, the sandbox retains a link to the real destination and installer writes can modify files outside the sandbox. A dry run must not preserve links that allow writes to escape; reject them or copy data into isolated regular files.

findings.title: Dry-run failures discard their diagnostic output
findings.description: The install runs with a buffered stdout sink, but buffered lines are replayed only after the install returns successfully. If it throws `InstallAbort`, the buffer is discarded; `installIde()` then returns exit code 1 without printing that buffered error. For example, a missing rules directory produces a failed dry run with no explanatory diagnostic. Replay the relevant buffered output when the install aborts, while still cleaning up the sandbox.
